newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end firm, helped by strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end firm, helped by strong dollar.

text.p: Swiss shares closed higher on Wednesday, supported by a firmer dollar, gains on Wall Street and several warrant issues on blue chips.
The broad Swiss Performance Index ended up 16.26 at 2,527.06.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index closed 22 points higher at 3,944.9.

Banks led the market higher as the likelihood of a boycott by Jewish organizations against Swiss banks decreased after Swiss government said it wanted immediate talks on using dormant accounts for a fund for Nazi victims.
Union Bank of Switzerland, closing 21 francs higher at 1,179, led the actives list.
Shares in Credit Suisse group and Swiss Bank Corp were also firmer.
Pharmaceutical concern Novartis gained 11 francs higher to 1,533.
Industrial shares had a good market in general, dealers said. Hopes for a cyclical upturn in Europe and the weak Swiss franc should support export-oriented shares.
Fischer, Rieter, Saurer, Arbonia, SIG, Schindler and Keramik Laufen closed all higher.
EMS Chemie closed steady in active trade.
Soffex trade saw rising volume in SMI futures.
January SMI futures rose 22 points to close at 3,946 on 5,750 contracts.
In options, Novartis was actively traded. The open interest in some UBS options was also high, dealers said.
